name: Crossing 4-3-3

slots.why: Distributes to the target men or full-backs; long kicking helps.
Attacking full-back overlaps the wide target man and supplies the crosses.
Central defender. Cover is the alternate.
Central defender on the right. Cover is the alternate, but only one Cover can be used.
Attacking full-back on the right, doing the same job as on the left.
Defensive central midfielder covers the space the full-backs leave when they overlap.
Supporting central midfielder links the defence to the forwards.
Box-to-box midfielder runs into the box to attack the crosses and second balls.
Wide target man (Support) holds the touchline, wins headers and gets the ball out for the overlapping full-back.
Wide target man (Support) on the right, doing the same job as on the left.
Target man (Support) attacks the crosses and holds up the ball.

description: A 4-3-3 where attacking full-backs overlap two wide target men, and the ball is crossed early to a central target man.
whyGood: Three tall forwards and two overlapping full-backs put many players in the box, and the crosses come from several angles.
whyThisShape: The two wide target men stand near the touchline and are supported by attacking full-backs who overlap them, so the team has two players on each flank. Early crosses go to the central target man and the far-post target man, so up to three players are in the box for each cross, and the midfield three cover the space the full-backs leave.
whenToUse: When you have two tall forwards who can play wide, a strong central striker, and full-backs who can cross, especially against defences that are short or slow to turn.
whenNotToUse: Against tall centre-backs who win the crosses, or against quick wingers, since both full-backs are pushed high and the space behind them is open.

instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Give the wide outlets space to receive and stretch the opponent without isolating every central passer.
instructionRationale.Slightly More Direct Passing: Reach the forward outlets earlier without turning every possession into a long ball.
instructionRationale.Hit Early Crosses: Deliver before the defensive line resets, using the target or forward runners already attacking the box.
instructionRationale.Overlap Left: Ask the left-sided receiver to consider the outside run; this requires a wide defender who can supply that run.
instructionRationale.Overlap Right: Ask the right-sided receiver to consider the outside run; this requires a wide defender who can supply that run.
instructionRationale.Higher Tempo: Move the ball before the opponent resets, using the receivers and runners supplied by the roles.
instructionRationale.Distribute Quickly: Release the forward outlets before the opponent recovers.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Flanks: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Floated Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.More Urgent Pressing: Challenge more often inside the selected engagement zone without making the settled press maximal.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Standard Line of Engagement: Defend from a middle block; the forward roles still determine which players challenge the ball.
instructionRationale.Take Long Kicks: Use the selected forward or wide outlets without demanding short build-up under pressure.

keyRequirements: Two tall wide forwards who win headers
Central midfielders who cover the flanks
setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
No forced Counter after a regain: the receiving and linking roles choose when to release the runners, rather than requiring every regain to become a break.
